summary: Minor children, disabled children, a disabled spouse and parents are guaranteed at least half of what they would inherit by law, whatever the will says (Civil Code art. 1069). A foreign resident's movables are governed by the law of residence and land by Kazakh law. Outside the Astana International Financial Centre there is no trust law; the AIFC offers private foundations.
reserved_share: Minor and disabled children, disabled spouse and disabled parents: at least one half of the share they would take on intestacy (Civil Code art. 1069).
foreign_law_note: Secondary sources say movables follow the law of the country of the deceased's residence and land follows the law of its location. I found no mechanism for a foreigner to choose their national law. Kazakhstan's 2005 Private International Law Law was not retrieved.
trust_note: Not on the HCCH status table. National law has only a contract of trust management (Civil Code); a common-law trust is not recognised outside the AIFC. The AIFC Foundations Regulations (Regulation 24 of 2019, in force 1 April 2019, amended 2023) allow a foundation with its own legal personality for charitable, non-charitable or named-person purposes. AIFC entities sit under English-law-based courts.
open_questions: Confirm the Private International Law Law's succession article and whether a foreigner may choose law.
Confirm AIFC rules on trusts, and whether AIFC foundations hold assets outside the centre for estate purposes.
Article 1069 text was not retrieved directly; the one-half fraction comes from a law-firm guide.
